checkpoints.description: [1/3] Plan: hardening pass - reject --frames 0 instead of silently running 1/120 frames; make the shared component codec reject unknown keys and unknown dataclass fields like the other 10 versioned loaders; add coverage for the two untested modules component_codec and library_trash

impact_assessment.why: The CLI accepted --frames 0 then a falsy check turned it into 1 frame (simulate/headless) or 120 (playtest) while reporting the coerced value, so an agent could not trust its own requested frame count. The shared component codec was the only versioned loader that silently dropped unknown keys, and an unknown dataclass field leaked a raw TypeError. component_codec and library_trash had no test file at all.
impact_assessment.benefits: Requested frame counts are honoured or rejected, never silently changed; component authoring typos fail loudly with the codebase's existing message shape; the two untested modules now have regression coverage.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: CLI argument validation and component_from_dict strictness; dependency: none new; concurrency: none; state: no persisted format change - existing valid documents still load.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first test per defect, verify every consumer (prefab, scene snapshot, scene/prefab library, editor) still round-trips, and run the full 6/6 gate plus the canonical simulate hash.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Hardening implemented and verified - --frames 0 rejected on all four modes (was silently 1 or 120); component_from_dict rejects unknown document keys and unknown dataclass fields as ValueError; new test_component_codec.py (10 tests) and test_library_trash.py (12 tests). 909 tests pass, canonical simulate hash unchanged

impact_assessment.why: Every actionable claim in reports/keystone-improvement-2026-11-08.md was verified against live source by execution: engine constructs InputMap() with no game hook at app.py:59, DEFAULT_BINDINGS lacks fire/reload/slot/jump, AssetRegistry.refresh never touches a scene while rebinding lives only in web/editor.py:965, apply_pose has no mask, Scene has one point_light slot, instancing keys on id(), plan draw_calls is a node count, widgets expose only panel/button, no VersionedStore, and ARCHITECTURE.md claims v0.46.0 while the package is 0.45.0 with no CHANGELOG or --version.
impact_assessment.benefits: A game can finally deliver its own live controls; hot reload rebinds any AssetRegistry consumer instead of only the web editor; version drift and missing changelog stop misleading cold-starting agents.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: additive GameModule hook and a new reload_assets helper plus CLI flag; dependency: none new; concurrency: none; state: no persisted format change - existing scenes and bindings still load.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep every change additive and optional, keep default paths byte-identical, pin each fix with a failing-first test, and verify the canonical simulate hash plus all 6 project gates.

[1/3] Plan: adversarial defect hunt on the public API - found and fixed a quadratic/O(n^4) texture preset cost with an unbounded allocation, and a lock bypass where set_node and set_selection_properties mutated locked nodes

impact_assessment.why: TextureData.pattern ran per-pixel Python loops (panel 180ms, rivets 288ms at 512x512, rivets O(size^4)) with no size bound, and a locked editor node could still be renamed, re-layered, re-tagged, hidden or bulk-edited because two handlers omitted the guard their siblings call.
impact_assessment.benefits: Procedural textures are linear in pixel count with a 16 MB ceiling; an editor lock now blocks every mutation path rather than most of them.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: lock now rejects two more actions; dependency: none new; concurrency: none; state: no persisted format change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Prove pixel-identical output for the perf rewrite against a reference implementation, extend the lock regression to enumerate the new paths, and verify no suite test relied on the permissive behaviour.
